newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Manuel sees S.African GDP up 2.5 percent in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Manuel sees S.African GDP up 2.5 percent in 1997.

text.p: South Africa's real gross domestic product (GDP) is expected to grow by 2.5 percent in 1997, down from 3.1 percent in 1996, Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said on Wednesday.
"This is a year of consolidation," he said in his budget speech. Real output in the primary sectors was likely to slow but the manufacturing sector should do better.
"The manufacturing sector, which should benefit substantially from supply-side measures, should expand considerably faster than in 1996."

At the same time the downswing in merchandise imports and strong export growth are expected to lead to a lower current account deficit in 1997 than in 1996, when it totalled 8.5 billion rand versus 10.2 billion rand in 1995.

"A continuation of the recovery in capital inflows which has occurred since the beginning of this year should result in a considerable capital account surplus over the current balance, resulting in an improvement of our foreign reserve position," Manuel said.

Consumer price inflation is expected to average 8.5 percent, somewhat higher than in 1996. But Manuel said the trend was expected to slow down during the course of the year as a result of a decline in the public sector borrowing requirement and a contraction in credit growth and money supply.
